guide.greenlantern.trench.title: The Trench
guide.greenlantern.trench:
Old enemies of Atlantis, the §4creatures of the Trench§r are a hostile people of the deep: gaunt, with pale eyes that glow in the dark, long claws and mouths full of needle teeth.

They don't just appear like zombies. §6They live in colonies§r, the Nests of the Trench, dug into the sea floor around Atlantis (three nests, some 200 blocks from the city). They hunt in packs, defend the nest and keep the villagers they capture there.

§6Away from Atlantis§r
The nests are dug once Atlantis is finished. From the city, swim away in any direction: you will know when you get there.
guide.greenlantern.trench_territory:
You can tell at once when you swim into the territory of the Trench:

§6The sea darkens§r
The water turns almost black and you see less far. It is the §4The Trench§r biome.

§6The fish vanish§r
Nothing lives there: fish flee or disappear (the Trench eats them all).

§6Noises from the caves§r
Clicks, creaks and far-off wails echo out of the caves.

§6Dead coral§r
The sea floor turns to dark rock, sculk and bleached dead coral, with bones sticking out of it.

Everything that enters the territory is hunted.
guide.greenlantern.trench_nest.title: The Nests
guide.greenlantern.trench_nest:
Everything Atlantis is not: black rock instead of white marble, bone and flesh instead of gold and glass, a few dim, warm glows instead of sea lanterns.

§6The pit§r
A jagged hole in the sea floor, its walls of deepslate, blackstone, basalt and sculk, crowned with black spires.

§6The ribcage§r
Giant arches of bone curve over the pit, with roots hanging down like tentacles.

§6The brood mound§r
In the middle of the pit, a mound of flesh and sculk studded with glowing egg sacs.

§6The chambers§r
Five caves run out of the pit walls into chambers of flesh and bone: that is where the cocoons with the captured villagers hang.
guide.greenlantern.trench_creatures:
§6In packs§r
Each nest has two packs: one circles inside the pit guarding the brood, the other patrols the territory. When a creature spots prey it screeches and the whole pack attacks.

§6Like sharks§r
Between strikes they circle their prey, each in its own place, then dart in to claw and bite.

§6The Brute§r
Bigger, slower and much tougher, with red eyes. Its screech darkens the sea around it (Darkness effect).

§6Fear of light§r
A lantern, torch, sea lantern, glowstone or the Green Lantern's ring in hand often makes them recoil instead of striking (the Brute is less afraid).

§6Out of the water§r
They lunge at the water's edge but go no further: out of the sea they dry out and get hurt.

§6Replacements§r
Dead creatures are slowly replaced from the deep, when nobody is watching.

§6Loot§r
Bones, ink sacs (sometimes glowing), prismarine shards and, from the Brute, nautilus shells.
guide.greenlantern.trench_captives.title: Captured villagers
guide.greenlantern.trench_captives:
The Trench captures villagers it finds in the water and carries them to the nests. Now and then a hunting party comes home with a new captive in its claws: kill the hunter on the way and the villager is free.

§6Cocoons§r
In the chambers of the nest, villagers are held in cocoons of translucent flesh, alive (they breathe through the membrane).

§6Rescue§r
Strike the cocoon a few times to tear it open. The villager comes out, breathes underwater for a few minutes, swims up to the surface and leaves emeralds in thanks.

Careful: attacking a cocoon calls the whole nest.
guide.greenlantern.trench_raids.title: Raids on Atlantis
guide.greenlantern.trench_raids:
Now and then, while someone is in Atlantis, a war party leaves one of the nests and attacks the city, led by a Brute.

§6The warning§r
A war cry echoes and the §4The Trench raids Atlantis§r bar appears, showing how many raiders are left.

§6The defense§r
The royal guard of Atlantis fights the invaders. Defeat them all and Atlantis drives off the raid; if it lasts too long, the war party withdraws into the deep.

In the mod's config (section §etrench§r) raids can be turned off or made more or less frequent.
